page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v5 is an EDSv5-family virtual machine configured with 64 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 48 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is bundled with 2458 GB of local SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression tasks fall within the average range, multi-core execution is strong, as evidenced by high scores in multi-threaded stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is robust, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidths ranking in the top 25%. However, the absence of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy machine learning workloads; while small and medium LLM inference tasks perform at average speeds, large 70B model text generation is weak, averaging only 2.72 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E64ds_v5 offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with a large local SSD on a dedicated hypervisor allocation. This profile is highly optimized for memory-intensive and data-heavy workloads. It is well-suited for relational databases, large-scale software compilation, multi-threaded data decompression, and high-throughput static web serving, where its strong multi-core processing and memory bandwidth can be fully leveraged.
